source_refs.note: Exercise 8.3, Question 7: book page 162 (PDF 167); answer key book page 302 (PDF 307): 2/sqrt(5) (agrees).

blocks.prompt: 7. Identify the following series as binomial expansion and find the sum: \(1 - \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{4}\right) + \frac{1 \cdot 3}{2! \cdot 4}\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^{2} - \frac{1 \cdot 3 \cdot 5}{3! \cdot 8}\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^{3} + \dots\)
blocks.explanation:
Terms ko ghaur se dekhiye: upar \(1 \cdot 3 \cdot 5\) jaise odd numbers ke products, neeche factorials, signs badalte hue, aur \(\tfrac{1}{4}\) ki powers. Yeh binomial series ki pehchaan hai.
Find kya karna hai? Woh \(n\) aur \(x\) jin se yeh \((1 + x)^{n}\) ki expansion bane, aur phir series ka jama.
Plan: neeche ke 4 aur 8 ko 2 ki powers likhna, \((1 + x)^{n}\) se milana, aur jama \((1 + x)^{n}\) ki value.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(1 - \frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{4}) + \frac{1 \cdot 3}{2! \cdot 4}(\frac{1}{4})^{2} - \frac{1 \cdot 3 \cdot 5}{3! \cdot 8}(\frac{1}{4})^{3} + \dots\) (kitab mein dot ka matlab multiply hai).
Humein find karna hai: yeh kis binomial ki expansion hai, aur is ka jama.
Tareeqa: Is series ko general series se milayenge:
\[(1 + x)^{n} = 1 + nx\]
\[+ \dfrac{n(n - 1)}{2!}x^{2}\]
\[+ \dfrac{n(n - 1)(n - 2)}{3!}x^{3} + \dots\]
Jab \(n\) aur \(x\) mil jayein to poori la-mehdood series ka jama seedha \((1 + x)^{n}\) hai.

Pattern pehchanein
\[4 = 2^{2},\quad 8 = 2^{3}\]
\[\dfrac{1 \cdot 3}{2! \cdot 2^{2}} = \dfrac{(-\frac{1}{2})(-\frac{3}{2})}{2!}\]
\[-\dfrac{1 \cdot 3 \cdot 5}{3! \cdot 2^{3}} = \dfrac{(-\frac{1}{2})(-\frac{3}{2})(-\frac{5}{2})}{3!}\]
Kyun: Neeche wale 4 aur 8 asal mein \(2^{2}\) aur \(2^{3}\) hain. Har odd number apne saath ek 2 le leta hai: \(\tfrac{1}{2}, \tfrac{3}{2}, \tfrac{5}{2}\). Teen minus ka product minus hai, is liye chauthi term minus wali hai; do minus plus, is liye teesri plus wali.
Dhyan dein: kitab ka '2!4' ka matlab \(2! \times 4\) hai, 24 nahi.

\(n\) aur \(x\) parhein
\[n = -\dfrac{1}{2},\quad x = \dfrac{1}{4}\]
\[nx = -\dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{1}{4}\ \checkmark\]
Kyun: Factors \(-\tfrac{1}{2}, -\tfrac{3}{2}, -\tfrac{5}{2}\) bilkul \(n, n - 1, n - 2\) hain jab \(n = -\tfrac{1}{2}\). Aur har term mein \((\tfrac{1}{4})\) ki power hai, to \(x = \tfrac{1}{4}\). Doosri term \(nx\) se bhi mil gayi.

Valid hai ya nahi
\[|x| = \dfrac{1}{4} < 1\]
Kyun: \(|x| < 1\) hai, is liye yeh la-mehdood series waqai \((1 + x)^{n}\) ki taraf jaati hai aur jama ka matlab banta hai.

Jama
\[\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{4}\right)^{-1/2} = \left(\dfrac{5}{4}\right)^{-1/2}\]
\[= \sqrt{\dfrac{4}{5}} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\]
Kyun: Negative power fraction ko ulta kar deti hai: \((\tfrac{5}{4})^{-1/2} = (\tfrac{4}{5})^{1/2}\). Phir \(\sqrt{4} = 2\).

Tasdeeq
\[1 - 0.125 + 0.0234 - 0.0049 = 0.8936\]
\[\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{5}} = 0.8944\]
Kyun: Sirf chaar terms ka jama bhi \(\tfrac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\) ke bahut qareeb hai; baqi terms farq poora kar deti hain.
